title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: Augustine on Pelagius — grace to the worthy; Prosper’s chronicle; Faustus — attracting mercy if given to the worthy
pass_a_gloss: So concerning Pelagius himself Augustine writes that he held that God gives this grace unto him who shall have been worthy to receive it, Cap. 14. De gestis Palaestinis. And Haer. 88. the same Father witnesses that the Pelagians’ error was, That the grace of God by which we are freed from impiety is given according to our merits. So also Prosper in the Chronicle at the year 414. writes, In this season Pelagius the Briton puts forth the dogma of his name against the grace of Christ, preaching that each one is ruled unto righteousness by his own will, and receives as much grace as he shall have deserved. Now let Faustus their leader speak for the Semipelagians, If the mercy of the attracting God is given unto the worthy, you mark that it is already also spent upon the endeavour of human service somehow, Lib. 1. cap. 17. A little after, In him whom you see attracting, he requires in every way one keeping the precepts, that by a certain little handle of will he who is called may be able to be grasped.
pass_b_english: So Augustine on Pelagius himself (De gestis Palaestinis 14): he held God gives this grace to whoever is worthy to receive it. And Haeresis 88: the Pelagian error was that the grace by which we are freed from impiety is given according to our merits. Prosper’s Chronicle for 414: in that season Pelagius the Briton put forth his dogma against Christ’s grace, preaching that each is ruled to righteousness by his own will and receives as much grace as he deserves. For the Semipelagians hear their leader Faustus (lib. 1, c. 17): If the attracting God’s mercy is given to the worthy, you see it is already also spent on somehow serving by human effort. A little later: in the one you see attracting, he requires in every way a keeper of the precepts, so that by a little handle of will the called may be grasped.
source_text: Sic de Pelagio ipso scribit Augustinus, eum nempe tenuisse, donare Deum hanc gratiam ei qui fuerit dignus accipere, Cap. 14. De gestis Palaestinis. Et Haer. 88. idem Pater testatur Pelagianorum errorem fuisse, Quod gratia Dei qua liberamur ab impietate, secundum merita nostra detur. Sic etiam Prosper in Chron. ad annum 414. scribit, Hac tempestate Pelagius Brito dogma nominis sui contra gratiam Christi exserit, praedicans, unumquemque ad justitiam propria voluntate regi, tantamque accipere gratiam quantum meruerit. Jam pro Semipelagianis loquatur Faustus illorum antesignanus, Attrahentis Dei misericordia si dignis datur, advertis quia jam et studio humanae utcunque servitutis impenditur, Lib. 1. cap. 17. Paulo post, In quem perspicis attrahentem, requirit omnimodis praecepta servantem, ut per quandam voluntatis ansulam comprehendi valeat qui vocatur.
